name: Warrant
comment: Grammar for the Warrant rule DSL, kept in sync with the parser (src/DSL/Parsing/WarrantParser.php) and lexer (src/DSL/Lexing/Lexer.php). Cross-schema references are implemented: KEYWORD(<predicate> for <handle> [with <context map>]) — e.g. can(create_timesheet for users(@context user_id)) and check(is_open('p') for pay_periods(@context id) with k = @context v). A handle is a schema name, optionally row-bound with a single `(<arg>)` selector and optionally naming the rows it selects with a trailing `as <alias>`; a can(...) may omit the `for <handle>` entirely, asking about another ability of the schema the rule is written on. Arguments may be literals, :name / ? bindings, @context <key>, @column <column> or @column <name>.<column> (a database column, qualified by a frame name when a rule can see more than one), or @sql "<sql>" (an arbitrary SQL fragment). If the DSL grows new tokens/keywords, add matching patterns here.

column-ref.comment: `@column <column>` or `@column <name>.<column>` — a database column reference, resolved to a grammar-wrapped column at compile time. One name is the column, on whatever rows the rule is already about; two name a frame (a schema key, or an alias a handle introduced with `as`) and then the column. The qualified alternative comes first so a frame name is not mistaken for a bare column (same line only).

sql-ref.comment: `@sql "<sql>"` — an arbitrary SQL fragment spliced verbatim (parenthesized) at compile time. Highlights `@sql`; the quoted body is tokenized by the string rules.
sql-ref.name: variable.language.sql.warrant

positional-binding.comment: A `?` placeholder binding, scoped like :name so both binding forms look alike.
positional-binding.name: variable.parameter.binding.warrant

schema-target.comment: `for <schema>` — both the header of a top-level `for <schema> { ... }` rule-set block and the `for <schema-handle>` inside a cross-schema can(...)/check(...). Highlights `for` as a keyword and the schema name that follows it as a namespace. Any optional row-binding `(@context id)` after the name is tokenized by the other rules. Same-line only (a match cannot span lines); when `for` and the name are on different lines, `for` falls back to the keyword rule below.

keywords.comment: The DSL's reserved words (Lexer::KEYWORDS). `can`/`check` also act as expression-position builtins for cross-schema references; they still scope as keywords here.
keywords.name: keyword.control.warrant

operators.comment: ! negation and * wildcard operators, plus `=` for the assignment in a `with key = value` context-mapping clause. A `?` is NOT here: it is a positional binding, matched by #positional-binding.
operators.name: keyword.operator.warrant

punctuation.comment: ( ) , punctuation, plus { } delimiting a `for <schema> { ... }` rule-set block.
punctuation.name: punctuation.separator.warrant
